content: TGM6, or Transglutaminase 6, is a protein in humans that is encoded by the TGM6 gene. The protein encoded by the TGM6 gene is a member of the transglutaminase superfamily. It functions by catalyzing the cross-linking of proteins and the conjugation of polyamines to proteins. Mutations in the TGM6 gene have been linked to spinocerebellar ataxia type 35 (SCA35), a neurodegenerative disorder. Additionally, alternative splicing of this gene results in transcript variants that encode different isoforms of the protein. Mutations in the TGM6 gene have also been implicated in the development of acute myeloid leukemia. To study the function of TGM6, model organisms have been utilized. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Tgm6tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was created at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the effects of TGM6 gene deletion.
